claim: Tony La Viña pointed to Loren Legarda’s legislative record, particularly her years of championing environmental causes.
source_context: DEFENDING LOREN: ADVOCACY NOT AN ALIBI, FRIENDSHIP NOT PROOF OF INNOCENCE Last Friday, I co-hosted TV5’s Storycon with Philippine STAR editor-in-chief Amy Pamintuan and veteran journalist Regina Lay. We had an interesting discussion with renowned law professor Atty. Tony La Viña, whom we invited for a live interview, about his decision to serve as spokesperson for Sen. Loren Legarda amid the controversies surrounding her and her son, Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste. Tony began his defense of Loren by saying that he has known her from way, way back. He pointed to the senator’s legislative record, particularly her years of championing environmental causes. In an earlier Facebook post, he cited Loren’s environmental laws, including the Clean Air Act and Renewable Energy Act, among others. He then used this record to argue that the allegations against Loren have “no basis.” This argument is as dim as Leandro’s solar projects. It is a non sequitur. So what if a politician has a long list of advocacies? It is not an alibi for plunder or abuse of power. A politician can champion the sun and trees, turtles, dolphins and all the animals in Noah’s Ark and still ransack the nation’s coffers. Following this logic, the large-scale corruption, extrajudicial killings and election cheating under former president Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo would likewise have “no basis” because she was a pro-life advocate who lifted the death penalty. The accusations against Sen. Pia Cayetano for spreading fake news through a spliced video of Akbayan Rep. Chel Diokno would similarly have “no basis” because she is a champion of reproductive health. And allegations of ghost and anomalous projects against Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano would have “no basis” because he is a devout Christian. After all, he is the “Ambassador of Jesus Christ.” But the most stupefying of Tony’s defenses of Loren and her son is his claim that they are “victims of political persecution.” Ah, yes. The same “political persecution” line now doing heavy duty in the political vocabulary of twice-impeached Vice President Sara Duterte. Please. Let us not insult those who actually suffered political persecution, such as ML Representative Leila de Lima who, as a senator, was unjustly and without any basis imprisoned by the Duterte regime for seven years. Whatever political intramurals Loren and her son may have with the administration, these do not erase, or even diminish, the serious allegations they face and the public’s legitimate demand for truth and accountability. Frankly, it would have been far more understandable and tolerable if Atty. Tony La Viña had simply said that he was choosing Loren’s side because she is a close friend. Period. Tony is free to stand by a friend, just as Loren is lucky to have a friend in him. Friendship may explain why one chooses to defend someone even if it does not prove the absence of wrongdoing. But to dress up a defense in weak arguments? Now that is something else. Advocacy does not immunize a politician from scrutiny or accountability. And friendship, however genuine, is not evidence of innocence.

articles.title: Coffee at Manila Polo Club
articles.description: COMMENTARY: Loren Legarda’s spokesperson, the self-proclaimed “human rights lawyer” Tony La Vin̈a, has been silent on the Manila Polo Club meeting even if the incident can be easily verifiable.
articles.text: Antonio Julian Montalván II is a Europe-based Filipino social anthropologist and heritage activist. By Antonio J. Montalvan II It was an invitation for coffee at 8 a.m. The host was a member of the exclusive Manila Polo Club inside Forbes Park. Sen. Loren Legarda was also a resident at Forbes’ No. 40 Cambridge Circle . It was her territory. The invitee was then the congressman representing Buhay party list in the House of Representatives, the former Manila mayor Lito Atienza. Why Atienza? From 2016 to 2019, he was the representative of the House Minority in the Committee on Legislative Franchises. Atienza was in the political opposition to the supermajority in the House of Rodrigo Duterte. Why the host invited him at the Manila Polo Club was intriguing. After settling down to their table, Legarda asked Atienza the forthright question forthwith. Lito I understand you are against the granting of a national franchise to my son’s company. There was no hesitation in exposing the meeting’s intention: a senator was lobbying a congressman for a bill benefitting the senator’s son. The conflict of interest was outright garapal . Atienza explained: I wasn’t really against. I just thought it wasn’t needed. A solar company can exist and operate without a franchise from Congress. So why is your son asking for a franchise, a national one at that? It will be like he will be the only one operating in the country, with the sanction of the Philippine government. The mother replied: Lito tulungan mo na lang. Magaling na bata yan. Matalino yan. Atienza: His intelligence is not the question. We need electrification. Solar power is one of the solutions. I am very careful in approving franchises that may not work in favor of the nation. Legarda: Well, I understand your position. But I want you to know that I am chairman of the Committee on Finance in the Senate. I can help you with a 10 million fund for any of your projects if you help my son. Atienza: Senadora, kung yan ang paguusapan, I’m out of it. Atienza said he then stood up but a common friend of theirs who was present and who acted as their go-between prevailed upon him. Atienza said the person was a former governor of Antique. Atienza listened again but in the end reiterated his position: I believe he doesn’t need a franchise . At this point of Atienza’s narration, it is clear that the purpose of the meeting was not coffee. It was to wine and dine him in the figurative sense. The event narrated by Atienza happened before the House passed in 2019 a national franchise for Leandro Leviste’s Solar Para sa Bayan. Atienza now claims he was right: with a small capitalization of only 1 million (later increased to 1 billion), Leviste would greatly benefit by selling the company. Legarda responded that the pay-off claim is utterly false, baseless and an unfair attack on her integrity. She has not elaborated on the Atienza narrative point by point. Her spokesperson, the self-proclaimed “human rights lawyer” Tony La Vin̈a, has been silent on the Manila Polo Club meeting even if the incident can be easily verifiable. articles.title: Loren Legarda fattens her dynasty
articles.description: In the certified list of candidates for Antique Representative, the name of Sen. Loren Legarda’s brother appeared as “Legarda, AA Inday Loren.”
articles.text: Antonio Julian Montalván II is a Europe-based Filipino social anthropologist and heritage activist. By Antonio J. Montalvan II What is it with Philippine politics that makes it so unapologetically and scandalously about self-interest in how to preserve one’s exclusive foothold on power? For many, that is a rhetorical question; the Filipino electorate knows the answer. But those who think they are God’s gifts to the Filipino people can never care less for rhetorical questions. Loren Legarda’s website is a superlative spotlight on what a gift she is to the nation—the planet rather. Loren Legarda’s life mantra has been for the Filipino people, the country, and the planet. She is a true Filipina at heart, passionately advocating for the protection of the rights of indigenous peoples and promoting arts and culture in the local and international arena. She started out in the public mind as a reporter of Radio Philippines Network (RPN) during the Marcos dictatorship. A later plum post came at ABS CBN where she was hired as co-anchor of The World Tonight newscast with Angelo Castro Jr. The network would later upgrade her as host of her own current events series The Inside Story. Her journalism career brought her accolades: the Gawad Cultural Center of the Philippines, the Catholic Mass Media Awards Hall of Fame, the Golden Dove Award of the Kapisanan ng mga Brodkasters sa Pilipinas, the Benigno Aquino Award for Journalism, and more than 30 other awards. The verdict was: her name recall was indubitable. That jumpstarted the political career of this “true Filipina at heart” in 1998 when she ran for senator under the Lakas-NUCD-UMDP party. Her presidential candidate was Jose de Venecia. She was the topnotcher of that senatorial race with 15 million votes. Nothing wrong with that. Twenty-seven years later, the altruism that all neophytes swear to in serving the country needs evaluation. The Loren Legarda we see today has mutated into a traditional politician who has alternated between the Senate and the House of Representatives to transcend term limits. And more. In the last elections, after she had served for one term as representative for the lone congressional seat of Antique, she fielded her younger brother Antonio Agapito “AA” Legarda to take over. Legarda herself claims she also keeps residence in Pandan, Antique, home of her maternal grandmother’s Gella family. For his first congressional run, AA Legarda registered his political alias as “Inday Loren.” How long has she been known truly as Inday Loren in Antique before she had run there in 2019 after her senate term had ended? Does she even speak Kinaray-a? In the certified list of candidates for Antique, the brother’s name appeared as “Legarda, AA Inday Loren.” Promptly, a resident of Bugasong town, Salvador Ungsod, petitioned the Comelec that this was a deception to Antique voters that it was Loren running. The prayer was to declare him a nuisance candidate. But as it is always in Philippine politics, having two family members in elective positions is not enough. Our democracy rests on the power, not of the people, but of presiding families over cities, provinces, and districts. And Loren Legarda has joined the drift of the fickle. What was the price of that budding dynastic ambition? In the present 2025 congressional race, AA Legarda is running for reelection. Loren had to sever ties with her political allies in Antique led by the Gov. Rhodora Cadiao who was eyeing the lone congressional seat because she had completed her three terms as governor. They had run on the same ticket in 2022. Loren had become a determined dynast. And why not? Imagine the combined pork barrel benefits of a senator and a congressman. Antique’s voters will have their hands full of campaign largesse. The 2022 presidential campaign was said to be particularly unkind to candidate Leni Robredo in Antique. Supporters were dismayed that the 18 municipal mayors were reportedly ordered not to extend any welcome to the vice president, including at the provincial capitol. But the Bongbong Marcos team was given permission to use the Evelio B. Javier Freedom Park. Javier was the martial law hero who was assassinated in cold blood by the forces of Antique kingpin and Marcos henchman Arturo Pacificador. Who gave the order for the cold welcome to Vice President Robredo? Antiqueños say the municipal mayors fear Loren. She was running in the Marcos-Duterte ticket. The coattail of the Edsa People Power she had originally run on was gone. And then for this present electoral race, a third family member will join the two Legardas. Leandro Legarda Leviste , the senator’s son, is running for the first congressional district of Batangas. Readers, judge for yourselves if Legarda Leviste needs a congressional seat. At 31 years old, the young Leviste is already worth P12B. He is CEO of the renewable energy firm Solar Philippines (that he claims he had patterned from Elon Musk; he had once invested in Tesla). He is also a sugar baron through the sugar firm Roxas and Company, Inc. (Central Azucarera de San Pedro in Nasugbu, Batangas) that he had saved from bankruptcy after buying 188.89 million shares. Last year, Leviste’s LL Holdings Inc. and Countryside Investment Holdings bought 10% of ABS CBN Corporation , making him the second largest shareholder of the media conglomerate after the Lopez family. It boggles the mind why a billionaire would lust for more power beyond what he already has. Protecting his business interests is a common script among Filipino politicians. See where the traditional politics of Leandro’s mother had landed on the lap of this wealthy young man? In July 2020, when the House of Representatives killed press freedom by denying the franchise of ABS CBN at the behest of Rodrigo Duterte , Representative Loren Legarda abstained. She cited a House rule that barred bill authors from voting otherwise (her bill, House Bill 6293 , would have renewed ABS CBN’s franchise). She claimed that the rule on conflict of interest barred her from voting to deny the franchise. But House sources say the rule only applies to members of the legislative franchises committee who are not ex-officio members. Legarda was ex-officio; she was Deputy Speaker, a House big shot. The mental gymnastics did not work. The public instead saw an alibi that her absence during the House hearing was because of fear of Rodrigo Duterte, who had once proclaimed Leandro Leviste as a future president of the Philippines . Loren Legarda would savor that future reality predicted by Duterte. The views in this column are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the views of VERA Files . articles.title: Legarda camp slams ‘political persecution’
articles.description: Environmental and constitutional lawyer Tony La Viña has described the plunder investigation involving Sen. Loren Legarda and her son, Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste, as “classic lawfare” and “political persecution.”
articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — Environmental and constitutional lawyer Tony La Viña has described the plunder investigation involving Sen. Loren Legarda and her son, Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste, as “classic lawfare” and “political persecution.” La Viña, who has stepped in as Legarda’s new spokesman, said the case was retaliation for Leviste’s public campaign against government corruption in late 2025. He also defended Legarda against allegations involving Leviste’s Solar Para sa Bayan Corp. (SPBC), stressing that the senator has no corporate ties to the company, did not receive government funds and did not vote for the passage of its non-exclusive franchise. “The senator does not own, run or take part in SPBC or any Solar Philippines company,” La Viña said. “Being a parent and being a senator does not in any way prove she benefited, acted improperly or committed a crime,” he added. La Viña also warned that the ombudsman’s approach to investigating unfulfilled renewable energy service contracts could discourage investment in the renewable energy sector. Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla yesterday confirmed that Legarda and Leviste had filed their counter-affidavits in response to plunder complaints involving alleged irregularities in solar energy projects amounting to P10.44 billion. “They have already filed their counter-affidavits. They filed them late, if I’m right, but we’re not going to get them on any technicality. We will still consider the counter-affidavits,” Remulla said at a press briefing. However, Remulla said the continued absence of the mother and son remains a stumbling block in the preliminary investigation as prosecutors may need to ask them questions. Legarda has been on medical leave since Aug. 3 and extended her leave until the first week of September. The ombudsman earlier flagged her extended medical leave, saying it raised suspicion. The mother and son left the country on separate flights, with Legarda traveling to France and Leviste flying to Hong Kong. Remulla said Legarda and Leviste were believed to be in Paris but had also traveled to Switzerland. The prosecution panel has 60 days to complete the preliminary investigation. On One News’ “Stotrycon” yesterday, La Viña could not say where the two are or whether they would return, or what Legarda’s health problem is. Investigators were considering legal measures to have them return to the Philippines, including the possible cancellation of their passports, to “preserve the integrity” of the proceedings before the anti-graft body and, if necessary, in court. “If there is a prolonged absence and we can consider them fugitives from justice, then that is the time that we will move for the cancellation of their passports,” Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano earlier said. Legarda has denied the allegations involving the solar power projects, calling them “false and baseless” and maintaining that no government money was involved. articles.title: Loren Legarda, hubby call it quits - report
articles.description: Former senator and broadcast journalist Loren Legarda has separated from businessman Jose Antonio Leviste, according to a newspaper report Thursday.
articles.text: Loren Legarda, hubby call it quits - report Former senator and broadcast journalist Loren Legarda has separated from businessman Jose Antonio Leviste, a newspaper reported Thursday. Legarda, who lost in the 2004 vice-presidential race to fellow TV broadcaster Noli de Castro, has two children with Leviste, a former provincial governor. It was the second marriage for both Legarda and Leviste. "I have been sustained by my strong faith in God and the support of family, friends, even my yaya (nanny)," Legarda was quoted as saying by the Philippine Star. According to the report, Legarda categorically denied that she has a boyfriend. She also said she was not thinking of remarrying. (She never said 'never', though, the news item said.) articles.title: Defending Loren: Advocacy not an alibi, friendship not proof of innocence
articles.description: Last Friday, I co-hosted TV5’s Storycon with Philippine STAR editor-in-chief Amy Pamintuan and veteran journalist Regina Lay.
articles.text: Last Friday, I co-hosted TV5’s Storycon with Philippine STAR editor-in-chief Amy Pamintuan and veteran journalist Regina Lay. We had an interesting discussion with renowned law professor Atty. Tony La Viña, whom we invited for a live interview, about his decision to serve as spokesperson for Sen. Loren Legarda amid the controversies surrounding her and her son, Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste. Not a few were surprised by Tony’s decision to become a mouthpiece for the mother-and-son tandem, particularly among those who know him as a staunch champion against corruption, the very issue that his clients now find themselves facing. Loren and her son are currently on an extended stay abroad which, if we are to believe them, is purely for health reasons, but which, rather remarkably, coincides with the ombudsman’s preliminary probe into their possible involvement in plunder and graft in connection with multibillion-peso solar projects. That is precisely why watching Tony argue so passionately for Loren’s side is painful. It is not so much that he has chosen to defend them. Tony is entitled to defend whomever he wishes. What is troubling are the glaring contradictions in the arguments he uses to do so. On our show, Tony began his defense of Loren by saying that he has known her from way, way back. He pointed to the senator’s legislative record, particularly her years of championing environmental causes. In an earlier Facebook post, he cited Loren’s environmental laws, including the Clean Air Act and Renewable Energy Act, among others. He then used this record to argue that the allegations against Loren have “no basis.” This argument is as dim as Leandro’s solar projects. It is a non sequitur. So what if a politician has a long list of advocacies? It is not an alibi for plunder or abuse of power. A politician can champion the sun and trees, turtles, dolphins and all the animals in Noah’s Ark and still ransack the nation’s coffers. Following this logic, the large-scale corruption, extrajudicial killings and election cheating under former president Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo would likewise have “no basis” because she was a pro-life advocate who lifted the death penalty. The accusations against Sen. Pia Cayetano for spreading fake news through a spliced video of Akbayan Rep. Chel Diokno would similarly have “no basis” because she is a champion of reproductive health. And allegations of ghost and anomalous projects against Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano would have “no basis” because he is a devout Christian. After all, he is the “Ambassador of Jesus Christ.” Tony then argued that Loren, who was then chair of the powerful Senate committee on finance, did not use her influence during the Duterte regime to secure an exclusive national solar franchise for Leandro. He said no documents show Loren as an officer, stakeholder or beneficiary of her son’s solar company. He also pointed out that the franchise passed through Congress without any hiccups. Again, a non sequitur. So what? A politician does not need to be legally listed as an officer, shareholder or beneficiary of a company to wield political influence for his or her own benefit, or for the benefit of family and friends. This was true in the Napoles pork barrel scam. It remains true in the multibillion-peso flood control corruption scandal. And just because a franchise passed both chambers of Congress does not make it aboveboard or establish that there was no influence-peddling and conflict of interest. If Tony can be fiercely critical of the controversial 2025 budget and the non-renewal of ABS-CBN’s franchise, both of which were approved by Congress, why can’t he exercise the same degree of scrutiny toward Leandro’s solar company which, after securing a congressional franchise, according to authorities, failed to deliver the promised power infrastructure, incurred P10 billion in unpaid obligations and was sold to another entity despite remaining incomplete? Tony would like us to believe that Leandro, who reportedly secured billions of pesos worth of projects at the age of 21, was simply a young and innovative entrepreneur. He appears convinced that Leandro was some kind of business whiz kid. Never mind that his extraordinary business acumen was hardly celebrated or even talked about in the business community. Nor was his genius particularly evident in his legislative work and debates with colleagues. Then again, perhaps we are simply too stupid, and too mortal, to comprehend the genius that Leandro is. But the most stupefying of Tony’s defenses of Loren and her son is his claim that they are “victims of political persecution.” Ah, yes. The same “political persecution” line now doing heavy duty in the political vocabulary of twice-impeached Vice President Sara Duterte. Please. Let us not insult those who actually suffered political persecution, such as ML Representative Leila de Lima who, as a senator, was unjustly and without any basis imprisoned by the Duterte regime for seven years. Whatever political intramurals Loren and her son may have with the administration, these do not erase, or even diminish, the serious allegations they face and the public’s legitimate demand for truth and accountability. Frankly, it would have been far more understandable and tolerable if Atty. Tony La Viña had simply said that he was choosing Loren’s side because she is a close friend. Period. Tony is free to stand by a friend, just as Loren is lucky to have a friend in him. Friendship may explain why one chooses to defend someone even if it does not prove the absence of wrongdoing. But to dress up a defense in weak arguments? Now that is something else. Advocacy does not immunize a politician from scrutiny or accountability. articles.text: Senate President Pro Tempore Panfilo “Ping” Lacson revealed that Senator Loren Legarda messaged him and asked him to give advise to her son, Batangas Representative Leandro Leviste. 📷༘ Lacson Team and Loren Legarda/Facebook MANILA — Senate President Pro Tempore Panfilo “Ping” Lacson revealed on Wednesday that Senator Loren Legarda messaged him and asked him to give advice to her son, Batangas Representative Leandro Leviste. 'It's so unfair': DOE chief says fine, contract termination vs Leviste firm unrelated to 'Cabral files' The request came amid criticisms thrown at Leviste, who made controversial statements regarding the so-called "Cabral files" and alleged P2 million Christmas bonus of congressmen, among others. “Nag-message nga sa akin si Senator Legarda. Na siyempre, pag bumabatikos ka, mag-expect ka rin na babalikan ka. Not necessarily totoo yung binabalik sa iyo pero ilalagay ka rin sa position na maging defensive ka.” He added that his heart goes out to Leviste, who should be thanked for telling the public what he knows. “Umiiyak daw kay Senator Legarda. ‘Bakit ako? Bakit ganito yung paninira nila sa akin? Eh alam ko si Senator Ping dumaan din siya sa ganyan.’ Pero mas matindi raw yung balik sa kanya,” Lacson said. articles.title: Loren Legarda takes oath as senator, vows to address climate change, pandemic issues
articles.description: Senator-elect Loren Legarda, who ran as a member of the Marcos-Duterte tandem's senatorial slate, took her oath at the Evelio B. Javier Freedom Park in San Jose de Buenaviste, Antique.
articles.text: Senator-elect Loren Legarda on Monday took her oath of office as a lawmaker of the 19th Congress in her home province of Antique, where she served as congresswoman for three years. The four-time Senator took her oath before Mag-aba, Pandan Barangay Captain Macario Bagac at the Evelio B. Javier Freedom Park in San Jose de Buenaviste. In her inaugural speech, Legarda reflected on the challenges that the country faces with the lingering effects of the “twin crises” of climate change and the COVID-19 pandemic. “How do we translate laws into substantial benefits that would extend to the farthest reaches of our 7,107 islands? How do we recover from the afflictions of the last few years, the twin crises of climate change and the pandemic? Trabaho at kabuhayan. Ito ang dapat nating patuloy na isulong lalo na’t hindi pa tapos ang ating laban sa kasalukuyang pandemya at sa krisis ng klima,” she said. (Work and livelihood. This is what we must continue to push for, especially that our fight against the pandemic and the climate crisis is not over.) Legarda said that local entrepreneurs and indigenous communities should be tapped to ensure that they would benefit from government programs such as the MSME Law, which she was a principal sponsor and author of. She said she will also promote green jobs and green skills in the country, and encourage people to engage in agriculture, forestry, horticulture, information technology, creative industries, and other careers that contribute to environmental and cultural preservation. Legarda further urged the House and Senate to ensure that the national budget is “a pandemic recovery budget, but one that is aligned with, and attuned to, the climate path.” “There is no recovery from COVID-19 unless we attack it on the issue of environment and climate. Also, rather than just ‘Building Back Better,’ we must focus firmly on the future and build right at first sight,” she said. “We now know that alongside investments in research and healthcare, we need to address the problem at its root: the destruction of nature. To save ourselves, we must save nature. Protecting nature is our fundamental, optimum, and most cost-effective line of defense against future pandemics and climate change,” she added. Legarda, one of the senatorial bets in eventual President-elect Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr.'s UniTeam slate, ranked second in the 2022 senatorial race with 24,264,969 votes. “It has been tremendously fulfilling, an ongoing journey, an enduring one because today marks the 22nd year as your lawmaker. I stand honored and proud before you to accept my mandate once again, to be your Senator for the fourth time, the most senior in terms of tenure,” she said. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: The resounding fall of Loren Legarda
articles.description: COMMENTARY: The UP Antiqueño statement hits the nail on the head. Loren Legarda is a reflection of a long career defined by opportunism.
articles.text: Antonio Julian Montalván II is a Europe-based Filipino social anthropologist and heritage activist. By Antonio J. Montalvan II It was 1998, the year of the presidential election that elected Erap Estrada. In the simultaneous senatorial election, a first-timer won a seat in the Senate, receiving the highest number of votes nationwide. Loren Legarda became only the second woman in Philippine history to top a senatorial election (14,933,965 votes). The first was Pacita Madrigal Warns in 1955 (2,544,716 votes). What captivated the electorate with Legarda? Her maximal exposure as a television anchor gave her a cut over the others. In ABS CBN, she had become news co-anchor with Angelo Castro Jr. in The World Tonight. The network had later made her host of her own current affairs series, The Inside Story. In 1998, no other senatorial candidate had the full advantage of daily name recall. As is usual in Philippine politics, politicians seek higher national positions because these roles offer greater control over state resources, deeper patronage networks, and long-term family influence. Higher offices control larger national budgets and public funds. The belief is they can use these resources to deliver direct favors, jobs and financial aid, thereby securing loyal voter bases. Senators and Congress representatives know this game so well: clientilism. The lure to establish dynasties begins here. For Loren Legarda, her ambition for higher office peaked after only six years as senator. It was rapid. In 2004, she ran as the vice presidential candidate to Fernando Poe Jr. It was also the first of her many jumps from one political party to another as political butterfly. The quintessential Legarda as traditional politician was born in 2004: one who changes political allegiance for power and convenience, shifting sides for survival. She lost the vice presidency in 2004 to Noli de Castro. She ran for the Senate again in 2007. In 2008, she became a fierce critic of Senate President Manny Villar and was part of the group that orchestrated Villar’s ouster. Two years later, she ran as vice president again under another party, the Nationalist People’s Coalition. Her presidential candidate was – but what else does a political butterfly do – Manny Villar. Twelve years as national politician is sufficient time to build one’s financial base. Of course the best political survival way is to conceal as hidden wealth what had been accumulated. In May 2013, just as Legarda was seeking reelection under the administration ticket, businessman and public interest advocate Louis Biraogo filed a complaint against her. Biraogo had alleged that Legarda had misdeclared her assets in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN). Biraogo showed evidence that in 2006, Legarda had bought a posh residential condominium unit in New York City at the cost of US$700,000. The Biraogo complaint had serious implications: violations of the anti-graft law and the code of conduct and ethical standards of public officials. Fifteen days later, Biraogo filed another complaint against Legarda in the Department of Justice. This time, it was for allegedly using a shell company to hide ownership of a Bali-inspired mansion in Forbes Park . Legarda herself identified the address at 40 Cambridge Circle when she issued printed invitations to a dinner she had hosted in 2009 for the visiting president of East Timor Jose Ramos Horta. Again, the mansion was undeclared in her SALN. Not surprisingly for political butterflies, as viewed in the backdrop of her current political affiliation in the Sara Duterte impeachment trial, Legarda had then accused fellow senator Alan Peter Cayetano as the hand behind the complaints. It was a plot to keep her from leading the senatorial elections. Grace Poe topped that elections, not Legarda. On June 6, 2013, the DOJ turned over the Biraogo complaints to the Ombudsman. Biraogo intimated to this writer that to this day, he had no idea why the Ombudsman had never acted on the complaints. Did Legarda receive protection as a senator allied with the second Aquino administration? The Ombudsman then was Conchita Carpio Morales. Today, we already know what butterfly wings Legarda had under the Rodrigo Duterte regime. In 2019, she began fattening her dynasty by fielding her brother Antonio Agapito as congressman of Antique, the ancestral home of her Gella maternal grandmother. Was she ever conversant in the Kinaray-a language? A dynast is clever with name recall. In the certified list of candidates for Antique representative, Legarda had packaged her brother as “Legarda AA Inday Loren.” Salvador Ungsod of Bugasong town petitioned the Comelec to declare AA Legarda as a nuisance candidate . Didn’t support home network, ABS-CBN Under Duterte who she allied herself with, we saw the Legarda who had become adroit at self-preservation. In the July 2020 voting to deny the franchise of ABS CBN at the behest of Rodrigo Duterte’s vendetta against the network, Legarda abstained. Legarda cited a House rule that barred bill authors from voting otherwise. She had authored House Bill 6293 that would have renewed the ABS CBN franchise. She had claimed that the rule on conflict of interest barred her from voting to deny the franchise. The House said otherwise – the rule applies only to members of the legislative franchises committee who are NOT ex-officio members. Legarda was ex-officio: she was House Deputy Speaker. Expect the same template for the Sara impeachment trial: Legarda’s prolonged absence for a purported “illness” will not entitle her to vote for the final verdict. She will hit two birds with one stone –self-preservation from tne wrath of both pro-Duterte and anti-Duterte forces. UP Antiqueño slams Legarda’s opportunism The UP Antiqueño statement hits the nail on the head. Loren Legarda is a reflection of a long career defined by opportunism . “We demand that Senator Loren Legarda and Congressman Leandro Leviste return to the Philippines to directly answer the plunder and graft complaints before the Office of the Ombudsman. Accountability for the People! Integrity in Governance!” The voice of the Karay-a people of Antique puts Loren Legarda and Leandro Leviste to shame. articles.title: Legarda urges climate-vulnerable nations to protect culture, heritage
articles.description: Senator Loren Legarda has called on climate-vulnerable countries to rethink outdated policies and adopt a more holistic and inclusive approach to climate action — one that protects not just lives and livelihoods, but also cultural identity, history, and heritage.
articles.text: Senator Loren Legarda has called on climate-vulnerable countries to rethink outdated policies and adopt a more holistic and inclusive approach to climate action — one that protects not just lives and livelihoods, but also cultural identity, history, and heritage. Speaking at the Climate Vulnerable Forum and V20 Finance Ministers (CVF-V20) meeting on Monday, Legarda said climate change poses a multidimensional threat, especially for nations that are on the frontlines of the climate crisis. "Climate change endangers all that you see and so much more: climate change imperils not only lives and livelihoods; it threatens to erase who we are," she said. The four-term senator and longtime climate advocate stressed that risk assessments must expand beyond economics and infrastructure to include cultural well-being — from ancestral homes and sacred sites to time-honored traditions. "It is this understanding that demands we broaden our definition of risk to fully encompass the cultural well-being of our people," she added. According to Legarda, extreme heat could cost the Philippines as much as ?466 billion annually by 2030. But more than the monetary loss, she warned of the intangible costs of losing cultural heritage, forced displacement from ancestral domains, and the gradual erosion of social cohesion rooted in shared traditions. She emphasized that preserving cultural memory and indigenous knowledge must be seen as central to climate resilience. "As legislators, we are more than mere policymakers; we are the stewards of our nation's future," the lawmaker said. "We must ensure that our laws reflect an unwavering commitment to both climate action and cultural preservation." The CVF-V20 is a coalition of 74 climate-vulnerable countries, including Bangladesh, Ghana, Sri Lanka, Barbados, and the Philippines. Together, they are developing Climate Prosperity Plans (CPPs) — ambitious national investment strategies designed to harness renewable energy, nature-based solutions, and financial innovation to foster inclusive development and climate resilience. The Philippines, which holds a founding role in the V20 group, has crafted its own Climate Prosperity Investment Memorandum, aligning climate goals with economic growth, clean energy transition, and local adaptation efforts. Legarda, principal author of the landmark Climate Change Act and champion of the People’s Survival Fund, urged fellow lawmakers to prioritize the implementation of the country’s Climate Prosperity Plan. "Let our collective efforts safeguard our precious cultural treasures, empower our resilient communities, and build a sustainable future for all Filipinos," she said. — Sherylin Untalan/RF, GMA Integrated News

articles.title: Legarda camp calls Ombudsman solar probe ‘political persecution’ | ABS-CBN News
articles.description: The camp of Sen. Loren Legarda and her son, Batangas 1st District Rep. Leandro Legarda Leviste, on Saturday accused the Office of the Ombudsman of pursuing a po
articles.text: Sen. Loren Legarda during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on Tuesday, July 21, 2026. Wendell D. Alinea, Senate Social Media Unit MANILA – The camp of Sen. Loren Legarda and her son, Batangas 1st District Rep. Leandro Legarda Leviste, on Saturday accused the Office of the Ombudsman of pursuing a politically motivated case against them over Leviste’s solar energy business. Atty. Tony La Viña, spokesperson for Legarda, said a review of the allegations showed no illegal or improper act by either the senator or her son. “After intensive review, I am convinced that she and her son have absolutely not done anything illegal and even improper with respect to the solar energy business of the latter,” La Viña said in a statement. “At worst, Leandro has been innovative and out-of-the-box as an entrepreneur. That should be rewarded, not punished,” he added. La Viña said that the case remains at the preliminary investigation stage and that no formal charges have been filed against Legarda or Leviste. Ombudsman: Plunder, graft raps vs Leandro Leviste, Loren Legarda over ‘solar empire’ to undergo preliminary probe Legarda extends medical leave until mid-September Ombudsman casts doubt on Legarda’s illness claim amid her extended 'medical leave' “It bears emphasizing that no formal charge has been filed against Senator Legarda or Representative Leviste,” he said. “Yet the Ombudsman’s public pronouncements convey the unmistakable impression that liability has already been assumed, notwithstanding that the matters involving them remain at the preliminary-investigation stage.” The Ombudsman launched a preliminary investigation into Legarda, Leviste and former Energy Secretary Alfonso Cusi over allegations involving Leviste’s solar energy companies and government contracts. Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla has alleged that Leviste’s companies failed to deliver promised solar power under contracts and described the issue as “ghost electricity.” The Ombudsman said the investigators found alleged abuse of legislative and regulatory powers in securing solar energy contracts. The probe stemmed from allegations involving Solar Para sa Bayan Corp. (SPBC), which was granted a 25-year congressional franchise in 2019 to develop renewable-energy microgrids in areas that were unserved or underserved. The Department of Energy (DOE) earlier accused the company of failing to fulfill obligations under the franchise and filed a complaint with the Department of Justice in May. In late August, the Ombudsman ordered Legarda and Leviste to submit counter-affidavits in response to the plunder and graft complaints. The DOE also filed a supplemental complaint earlier this month in an estafa case against Leviste and two SPBC officials, according to the department’s legal officer. Legarda has previously denied the allegations, calling them “utterly false and baseless” and saying she has not received any communication from the Ombudsman. ‘RESPONSIBILITY IS PERSONAL’ La Viña rejected attempts to connect the senator to Leviste’s companies simply because they are mother and son. “The Senator does not own, run, or take part in Solar Para sa Bayan Corporation (SPBC) or any Solar Philippines company. There are no corporate documents showing her as a shareholder, officer, or beneficiary,” he said. “Saying she’s connected to the business only because she’s the mother of a private businessman is pure invention.” La Viña said the senator’s relationship with Leviste should not be treated as evidence of wrongdoing. “Responsibility is personal,” he said. “Senator Legarda should not be shielded from scrutiny because Leviste is her son. But neither should motherhood become evidence against her.” He also disputed claims surrounding the congressional franchise, saying it was non-exclusive and did not provide government subsidies. “Senator Legarda did not vote for its passage,” La Viña said, adding that the franchise was never sold. He argued that the franchise could not be fully implemented because the DOE did not issue the implementing rules or identify the areas where it could operate, as required under the law. POLITICAL PERSECUTION? La Viña also argued that the scrutiny of Leviste’s solar ventures intensified after the lawmaker publicly exposed alleged corruption in late 2025. He claimed a series of allegations and investigations into Leviste’s projects emerged afterward. “The timing speaks for itself,” La Viña said, describing the situation as “classic lawfare, the weaponization of the law for political purposes.” “What is going on is clearly political persecution,” he said. “It has always been wrong. And it must stop now.” La Viña also defended Leviste’s business activities, saying unsuccessful implementation of an entrepreneurial idea should not automatically be treated as criminal conduct. “Leandro introduced new ideas and approaches to fast-track the energy transition, and there may have been policy gaps that prevented the successful implementation of some of those ideas,” he said. “But that is not a criminal act.” RELATED VIDEOS:

articles.title: Legarda grills Garin on DOE's action plan amid Middle East conflict | ABS-CBN News
articles.description: Senator Loren Legarda on Tuesday grilled Energy Secretary Sharon Garin for her agency's action plan as the Philippines feels the impact of the ongoing Middle Ea
articles.text: Energy Usec. Sharon Garin attends the Finance Subcommittee E's public hearing on the proposed 2024 budgets of government owned- and controlled corporations (GOCCs), namely National Power Corporation, Philippine National Oil Company, and the Power Sector Assets and Liabilities Management Corporation on September 22, 2023. Joseph Vidal, Senate PRIB handout/File MANILA -- Senator Loren Legarda on Tuesday grilled Energy Secretary Sharon Garin for her agency's action plan as the Philippines feels the impact of the ongoing Middle East conflict, describing the circumstance now as a "crisis." During the Senate Proactive Response and Oversight for Timely and Effective Crisis Strategy (Protect) committee hearing, Senator Win Gatchalian, its chairperson, asked Garin what would be the worst case scenario and the Department of Energy's (DOE) contingency plan should oil supplies run out and the conflict escalates. Garin told senators, "the worst case is we run dry, the country runs dry." "Ang good news diyan, we have about a month and a half to prepare for this. So ang contingency – that is why we are looking for other suppliers. We have to talk to the countries where we haven't talked to before para sila ang mag-supply," the energy chief said. She added that they are already talking to the United States and India on this matter and would work on this "in the next two weeks." Senator Loren Legarda – who criticized Garin's absence at the first part of the hearing – circled back to this statement, and pushed the energy secretary to respond to questions regarding their contingency and preparations. READ: Senators fume at absent energy chief, score admin for alleged lack of urgency, plans This is needed, she said, so government agencies could prepare for other scenarios related to the Middle East conflict. "Sinabi ng DOE we can actually run dry, tagtuyot– mauubusan. Ilan na lang. Pakipaliwanag anong ibig sabihin, 'the worst case is that our country runs dry.' Pakipaliwanag ang tagtuyot sa sambayanang Pilipino para kami maintindihgan namin ang paghahandang dapat gawin," Legarda told Garin. "Kung ganyan ang sinasabi ng DOE, hindi pa ba yan krisis? Ayaw pa ba talagang yugyugin ang utak ng mga tao sa gobyerno para tanggapin na tayo ay nasa krisis at sinasabi na we will run dry. Pakipaliwanag po," the senator added. Garin, for her part, said this means "we run out of fuel and gasoline and diesel." In the middle of her explanation, Legarda cut her, and said the secretary only provided the direct translation and not an explanation of what she meant. "English yung sinabi niyo. Sinalita niyo yung translated sa Filipino. Ibig kong sabihin is paliwanag, hindi explanation. What I want DOE to say is the implications. What does running dry mean in terms of the farming, fisherfolk, and the jeepney driver? What are the implications insofar as agriculture, the transport sector, insofar as what are your action plans?" Legarda fumed. Garin then detailed its impact on electricity and fuel, which she said could affect gas stations, islands' power supply, and greatly impact the transport sector. "PNOC, a government corporation, is looking for alternative routes other than those in Middle East. Yun ang isang intervention namin. We are willing to buy as long as there is enough supply in the Philippines. Sine-secure ang supply. That's our first and main objective," said the energy chief. But Legarda was not convinced and reverted to Garin's statement about the possibility of the Philippines "running dry" of fuel, emphasizing that government agencies have only given "motherhood statements" on what they would do should this happen. "Ang gusto kong marinig sana: impact if we run dry. Transport stops. Ano ngayon ang action plan, DOTr?... I don't think they are prepared for that. Perhaps in the second hearing, they can be more prepared and not come late," said Legarda.

articles.title: Legarda camp disputes P10.4-B basis of Ombudsman probe, says no gov’t funds involved | ABS-CBN News
articles.description: The camp of Senator Loren Legarda on Monday disputed the basis of the Ombudsman’s P10.44-billion plunder and graft probe against the senator and her son, Batang
articles.text: Sen. Loren Legarda during the third day of the impeachment trial on Wednesday, July 8. Joseph B. Vidal, Senate Social Media Unit/File MANILA — The camp of Senator Loren Legarda on Monday disputed the basis of the Ombudsman’s P10.44-billion plunder and graft probe against the senator and her son, Batangas 1st District Representative Leandro Leviste, saying that no government funds were released to his solar ventures. Tony La Viña, spokesperson for Legarda, questioned the inclusion of the senator in the case, saying there was no evidence she used her position to help her son secure renewable energy contracts. “This is political. There are no criminal acts that are being alleged here,” La Viña said in an interview with ANC’s Headstart. The remarks came after Legarda and Leviste filed their respective counter-affidavits in response to the Ombudsman’s preliminary investigation into alleged irregularities involving solar energy projects. Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla earlier said the cases against the mother and son involve more than P10 billion in alleged obligations linked to uncompleted solar projects. ‘NO GOVERNMENT MONEY INVOLVED’ 1st District of Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste speaks to the members of the press after the ratification of the bicameral conference committee report on the proposed 2026 national budget during a plenary session on Monday, December 29, 2025. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News La Viña maintained that plunder cannot apply because, according to him, the solar projects did not involve the release of government funds to Leviste. “Sa lahat ng kontrata ni Leandro, walang pera nilabas ang gobyerno,” he said. La Viña also rejected allegations that Leviste created a monopoly in the renewable energy sector, pointing to the number of service contracts awarded to his companies compared with the total number of renewable energy contracts. He said Leviste had 26 renewable energy service contracts out of 517 solar service contracts, or roughly 5 percent. Across the broader renewable energy sector, he said there were about 1,290 service contracts, with Leviste accounting for only about 2 percent. "Dito walang government funds, walang government property, at walang monopoly," he said. "You cannot call 5 percent of service contracts a monopoly even if you do not, which is not true." The Ombudsman has alleged that corporations linked to Leviste and Legarda obtained multiple exclusive solar energy service contracts, resulting in what it described as a virtual monopoly and alleged “ghost electricity.” Remulla previously said the government suffered because some of the contracted renewable energy capacity was not delivered. P24-B PENALTY La Viña also sought to distinguish the Ombudsman case from the Department of Energy (DOE)’s penalties involving Solar Philippines Power Project Holdings Inc. (SPPHI). The DOE initially announced penalties totaling around P24 billion against Solar Philippines over failure to meet commitments under renewable energy service contracts. The agency later cited a final bill of around P10 billion for the company. La Viña said the P24-billion figure was not a penalty personally imposed on Leviste and stressed that he is no longer the majority owner of SPPHI. “That is owned now by Meralco,” he said, adding that Leviste may only retain a minority stake. He also said Leviste’s own companies had incurred fees for projects that were not delivered, but claimed these amounted to less than P100 million and had already been paid. The DOE has previously said it terminated contracts covering roughly 12,000 megawatts of renewable energy capacity due to nonperformance. It has also referred the matter to the Office of the Solicitor General and the Department of Justice for possible legal action. As of early September, the DOE said it had recovered only P80 million from the P24-billion penalty imposed on SPPHI. “There’s no evidence of any kind of influence that she did for Leandro to get these contracts or this franchise,” he said. Leviste defends firm after P24-B fine The Ombudsman announced in July that it would pursue preliminary investigations into plunder and graft allegations against Legarda and Leviste over alleged irregularities involving solar energy contracts. The agency said the probe would examine allegations that the mother and son conspired to obtain contracts and created a virtual monopoly in the renewable energy sector. The DOE separately filed a complaint against Leviste and several officials of Solar Para sa Bayan over alleged failure to fulfill obligations under a congressional franchise for renewable energy microgrids. WHERE IS SEN. LEGARDA? The Committee on Culture and the Arts chairperson Sen. Loren Legarda met with cultural agencies and advocates on how the proposed department could effectively promote and protect Philippine culture and heritage, while addressing concerns regarding its structure and mandate on Wednesday, February 4, 2026. Joseph B. Vidal / Voltaire F. Domingo, Senate Social Media Unit La Viña also defended Legarda’s continued medical leave, saying the senator was following Senate rules and needed treatment for her illness. “Hindi sila nagtatago,” he said. “Actually hindi ko tinatanong kung nasaan sila. Ang alam ko lang po, tulad ng official na alam ng Senado, ay naka-medical leave si Senator Loren.” "Alam naman ng mga Senate colleagues niya kung anong dinadaanan niya na sakit. So that is her right to get the right medical treatment that she needs." The Ombudsman had earlier questioned the extended overseas absence of Legarda and Leviste amid the investigation. La Viña said he believes the complaints amount to “lawfare” or the weaponization of the legal system for political purposes. “I believe in the rule of law. And this is not the rule of law. This is weaponization of the law for political purposes,” he said. articles.text: The Office of the Ombudsman is investigating Senator Loren Legarda and her son, Batangas Representative Leandro Leviste, in connection with P10-billion plunder and graft complaints due to the alleged failure of his renewable energy firm to provide solar power as provided under its congressional franchise. In a press conference on Friday, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said, "Talagang nag-suffer tayo dahil sa ginawa. Kinuha nila 'yung exclusive contract ng solar [power contracts]. In a statement, Legarda maintained her innocence. “All my public life since 1998, I have always upheld my integrity, which I value dearly. This baseless allegation is a smear on my person that is totally undeserved,” she said. “We have not received any communication from the Office of the Ombudsman regarding the reported preliminary investigation, but I can categorically state that the reported accusations are utterly false and baseless. No public funds were involved. We are prepared to bring out the truth,” she added. Legarda then urged the public to be discerning, “especially in light of the timing and nature of these allegations.” “We remain confident that once the facts are laid bare, we will be vindicated and our names cleared,” Legarda added. — VDV/NB GMA News

articles.title: TOWNS Foundation disappointed with Loren Legarda's political decisions
articles.description: A group of women awardees for their outstanding service to the nation has expressed disappointment over the political stance on key issues of their fellow awardee, Senator Loren Legarda.
articles.text: The Outstanding Women in the Nation's Service (TOWNS) Foundation Inc. has expressed disappointment over the political stance on key issues of Senator Loren Legarda, a TOWNS awardee. In a statement, TOWNS said it hoped Legarda would be able to "reflect deeply on whether her recent actions honor the values for which she was recognized as a TOWNS awardee." The group aired its "profound disappointment" amid Legarda's move to "align with forces perceived to place political protection above truth, accountability, and justice," which it said "risks weakening public trust in democratic institutions." "The consequences go beyond politics. They diminish public faith in leadership, deepen cynicism among the youth, and damage the credibility of Philippine democracy before the global community. At a time when nations are measured not only by economic strength but by the integrity of their institutions, silence or compromise from respected leaders carries a heavy cost," TOWNS said. GMA News Online has reached out to Legarda's office for comment and will publish it as soon as available. Legarda was one of the 13 senators who voted in favor of Senator Alan Peter Cayetano as the new Senate President last May 13, in a surprise leadership change ahead of the transmittal of the articles of impeachment against Vice President Sara Duterte. Legarda received the TOWNS Award in 1995 for her excellence in media. In its post, the foundation said TOWNS women are expected to stand firm in crucial moments of the nation's history. "Our distinction is not based solely on achievement, but on courage of conscience, the willingness to defend what is right even when it is difficult or unpopular. We are called to place country above alliances, principle above expediency, and service above self-interest," it said. "The Senate's duty is not merely to enact laws, but to uphold the Constitution and ensure that no public official stands above accountability. History will remember not those who remained comfortable with power, but those who chose integrity when it mattered most," it added. TOWNS Foundation said it remains hopeful Legarda would respond positively. "The harm done to public trust and to the nation's moral standing need not be permanent. She still has the opportunity and the responsibility to help restore confidence in democratic institutions by choosing the path of constitutional fidelity, justice, and moral leadership," it said. "We continue to hope that she will rise to that challenge, not only for her own legacy, but for the country she once inspired many to serve," it added. Earlier, the student council of Assumption College San Lorenzo backed a petition for the removal of Legarda’s portrait from the school’s Wall of Empowered Women. “While her past contributions are acknowledged, her recent political actions no longer reflect the values that Assumption upholds,” the council had said. —LDF GMA News

Maria Tan & Mark Demayo, ABS-CBN News MANILA ( UPDATED ) — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and Bureau of Immigration (BI) confirmed Friday that Sen. Loren Legarda and her son Rep. Leandro Leviste left the Philippines separately on Aug. 2, Sunday, days after the Ombudsman announced a plunder investigation against the two. Ombudsman: Plunder, graft raps vs Leandro Leviste, Loren Legarda over ‘solar empire’ to undergo preliminary probe The BI said they allowed Legarda and Leviste's exit because the two have no derogatory record. ABS-CBN News sources said Leviste flew to Hong Kong, while his mother was on her way to Europe. The source added that Leviste's travel authority was effective from July 26 until Sept. 24, with several destinations in Asia, America, and Europe. The Office of the Ombudsman last week announced it would file plunder and graft complaints for preliminary investigation against Leviste, Legarda, and former energy secretary Alfonso Cusi over the congressman’s “solar empire.” Legarda had said the allegation "is totally undeserved." Sen. Erwin Tulfo later disclosed that Legarda filed for medical leave from August 3 to 5, 2026. “Nagpaalam po yata naman, may leave of absence po si Senadora Loren, in fairness to her medical leave po. Kausap po namin ni SP, yung aming executive secretary, sabi naman nag-file po si Senadora Loren,” Tulfo told reporters in an interview following his meeting with Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla and Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian Friday, August 7. “Kaya nga po, nung hearing po ng kuwan, wala po siya. Absent po siya,” he added. Asked if Legarda would be back next week, Tulfo said he hoped so, but he had no verified information. “Hopefully po, pabalik po siya. Wala naman ho binanggit kung anong klase. Basta sinabi lang ho, medical need,” the senator said. 'MEDICAL LEAVE' Legarda, meanwhile, said she filed a medical leave in accordance to Senate rules. She urged the public to avoid speculation regarding her reasons for leaving. "I confirm that I filed a formal medical leave with the Senate covering August 3 to 5, 2026, in accordance with Senate rules," said the senator in a statement. "I ask the public not to draw unwarranted conclusions from my travel or link it to the recent false and baseless allegations, which undeservedly besmirch a reputation that I have built over decades of public service." RETURN Ombudsman Jesus Crispin "Boying" Remulla, for his part, believes Legarda and her son Leviste will come home. “Tingin mo tatakasan talaga nila? I don’t think tatakas sila. Babalik ‘yun. Baka gusto nilang umuwi nang nakaposas pag ‘di sila bumalik, ‘di ba?” Remulla said in a press briefing Friday, August 7. Last month, the anti-graft body said it would file plunder and graft complaints for preliminary investigation against Legarda, Leviste and former energy secretary Alfonso Cusi over the congressman’s “solar empire.” They will also face a complaint for violating the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees. articles.title: Rodrigo Duterte arrest not about vengeance -de Lima
articles.description: Former Senator Leila de Lima said what mattered most about former President Rodrigo Duterte's arrest was that justice was finally within reach for the victims of extrajudicial killings.
articles.text: While the arrest of former President Rodrigo Duterte for crimes against humanity was "deeply personal" for former Senator Leila de Lima, she emphasized that what mattered most was that justice was finally within reach for the victims of extrajudicial killings. "For almost seven years, I was imprisoned on fabricated charges, accused of crimes I did not commit—all because I dared to speak out against Duterte’s drug war," De Lima said in a statement on Tuesday. "While I was behind bars, thousands of Filipinos were killed without justice, their families left to grieve with no answers, no accountability." "Today, Duterte is being made to answer—not to me, but to the victims, to their families, and to a world that refuses to forget. This is not about vengeance. This is about justice finally taking its course." De Lima, one of Duterte’s fiercest critics, was elected senator in 2016. In 2017, she was arrested and accused of involvement in the illegal drug trade at the New Bilibid Prison during her tenure as Justice Secretary. The cases filed against her were dismissed in 2024 . On Tuesday, authorities arrested Duterte for crimes against humanity following a warrant issued by the International Criminal Court, according to the Presidential Communications Office. De Lima stressed that it was time for Duterte to be held accountable for his controversial anti-illegal drug campaign, which claimed the lives of over 6,000 drug suspects, according to government records. Human rights organizations, however, estimate the death toll may have reached 30,000 due to unreported incidents. "I faced my case knowing I was innocent. I stood before the courts because I had nothing to hide. Duterte now has to answer for his actions—not in the court of public opinion, but before the rule of law," De Lima stated. "This is how justice should work—those in power must be held to the same standards as everyone else." "To those who have fought this long and difficult fight—your voices mattered, your courage mattered, and today, the pursuit of justice continues." — DVM, GMA Integrated News

articles.title: De Lima confronts Duterte over drug lord tag: 'Absolutely false'
articles.description: Former senator Leila de Lima on Wednesday called out former President Rodrigo Duterte for allegedly painting her as the "mother of all drug lords," saying he just used her as a scapegoat for the illegal drug menace.
articles.text: Former senator Leila de Lima on Wednesday called out former President Rodrigo Duterte for allegedly painting her as the "mother of all drug lords," saying he just used her as a scapegoat for the illegal drug menace. "That [allegation] is absolutely false. That is fictitious. They filed cases against me, consummation in illegal drug trade, amended it to conspiracy to [commit illegal drug trade], absuwelto na po ako sa tatlo. Wala po akong kinalaman sa illegal drugs," De Lima said before the House QuadComm probe on the drug war. (That [allegation] is absolutely false. That is fictitious. They filed cases against me, consummation in illegal drug trade, amended it to conspiracy to [commit illegal drug trade]. I've been cleared in three cases. I don't have anything to do with illegal drugs.) De Lima made the response after Duterte said he agreed with authorities quoted in a news report who tagged De Lima as the mother of all drug lords, saying that "I want to congratulate them for making that statement." During the early months of the Duterte administration, former deputy directors of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Reynaldo Esmeralda and Ruel Lasala filed complaints against De Lima for violation of Republic Act 9165 or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act, claiming that the senator was the " mother of all drug lords ." However, De Lima told the House joint panel that "They used me as a propaganda so they can use a prominent figure to be the center of attention here and abroad, that this woman is the mother of all drug lords." De Lima said her accusers, which included convicts and former government officials, have all ultimately retracted their allegations against her. "Binawi nila lahat [ng sinabi nila]. I was cleared in three drug cases, underwent through the process, kahit mahirap, masakit, kinulong nila ako ng seven years, and they cannot take it back due to the mastermind of my persecution, implemented by then-Justice Secretary Vitaliano Aguirre at iba pang kumausap sa mga nagtestigo sa akin with absolute slanderous accusation," De Lima said. (They retracted everything they said. I was cleared in three drug cases, underwent through the process, even though it was tough, painful. They jailed me for seven years. And they cannot take it back due to the [actions of the] mastermind of my persecution, implemented by then-Justice Secretary Vitaliano Aguirre and others who spoke with individuals who stood as witnesses against me with absolute slanderous accusations.) De Lima, who also led the probe on drug war killings during her stint as senator, spent nearly seven years in prison before being cleared of the drug charges. Last June, a Muntinlupa court granted her demurrer to evidence, effectively dismissing her third and final drug case . The former senator was freed on bail in November 2023 after being detained in Camp Crame since February 2017 over drug allegations. Her first acquittal came in February 2021 when the Muntinlupa City RTC-Branch 205 junked one of her three cases. In May 2023, the Muntinlupa RTC Branch 204 acquitted De Lima and Ronnie Dayan , her co-accused and former bodyguard, of an illegal drug trading charge on the ground of reasonable doubt. Earlier, a Quezon City court also dismissed De Lima’s two disobedience cases. — VDV, GMA Integrated News

articles.title: De Lima blasts 'remorseless' Duterte: 'You will answer for your crimes' | ABS-CBN News

articles.text: MANILA — Former Sen. Leila de Lima on Tuesday responded to former President Rodrigo Duterte's remark that she should just "find her peace" instead of seeking accountability for her "bogus" drug cases. • Duterte laughs off De Lima quest for justice, threatens ICC anew De Lima has vowed to sue Duterte administration officials who she blamed for her 7-year long detention. Wag kang kumalikot ng away kasi pagsisihan mo yan. Anong babawiin mo sa akin?" De Lima said Duterte will be held accountable for his crimes. "So let him revel in his perverted sense of machismo. But at the end of the day, he will be made to answer for his crimes. I have shown my respect for the rule of law, no ifs and buts. Does he?" De Lima said. articles.title: De Lima: Marcos administration ‘breathing room’ from Duterte’s ‘authoritarian regime’
articles.description: The administration of President Marcos provides a “breathing room” from the “authoritarian regime” of former president Rodrigo Duterte, according to former senator Leila de Lima.
articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — The administration of President Marcos provides a “breathing room” from the “authoritarian regime” of former president Rodrigo Duterte, according to former senator Leila de Lima. “Under BBM, we are given the opportunity to make use of a democratic space in transition from the authoritarian regime that was Duterte’s,” De Lima said in her speech before the Foreign Correspondents Association of the Philippines (FOCAP) at The Manila Hotel on Thursday. “This is a breathing room from the seven years of nightmare that we thought was all over in 1986 and never to return again. But it did,” she added. In an excerpt of De Lima’s speech uploaded by News5, the former senator also said Marcos brought back the normal order. “For the elite, therefore, Marcos is a blessing. He brought the rent-seeking order back to its favored normal and stable character, where everyone in the system gets a chance to partake,” she said. While the current administration is downplaying the significance of the 1986 people power revolt, representatives from various groups vowed to mobilize thousands of people for the commemoration of the bloodless uprising that toppled the late dictator Ferdinand Marcos Sr. Raymond Palatino, secretary general of Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan), said they expect at least 5,000 to attend the activities related to the 38th anniversary of the revolt tomorrow. The figure is lower than the 8,500 police officers the Philippine National Police (PNP) will deploy to secure the venues in Metro Manila and Cebu. Unlike previous years, the Marcos administration did not declare the anniversary of the revolt that toppled his father a special holiday. Various groups under the No to Cha-cha Network are all set for the rally and mass tomorrow to mark the 38th anniversary of the uprising. They will also hold demonstrations against Charter change. Under the theme “Tuloy ang laban ng EDSA! Biguin ang Chacha!” thousands of Filipinos are expected to join the rally. The assembly time was set at 2 p.m. along EDSA near Connecticut street. At around 3:15 p.m., the participants will march towards the EDSA Shrine. Among the confirmed speakers at the event is De Lima, who spent nearly seven years in jail on drug charges during the administration of former president Duterte. De Lima and other members of the opposition such as Sen. Risa Hontiveros, Albay congressman Edcel Lagman, former senator Bam Aquino, former presidential peace adviser Ging Deles and human rights lawyer Chel Diokno attended a mass at the EDSA Shrine on Friday commemorating the revolution. Militant groups also held demonstrations which they dubbed as Black Friday protests in Quezon City and Manila. Among these are the Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas and Kilusang Mayo Uno. After the rally, a mass will be held at the EDSA Shrine at 6 p.m. to be officiated by Catholic Bishops’ Conference of the Philippines president Bishop Pablo Virgilio David. In a joint statement, 123 organizations and 20 individuals declared their opposition to Charter change, stressing it is an unnecessary, divisive and expensive initiative aimed mainly at entrenching those in power. “An elite few have maintained, if not strengthened, their grip on our economy and political structures. Widespread poverty and injustice remain. Cha-cha does not address these problems,” they said. Col. Jean Fajardo, the PNP’s chief publicist, maintained their security coverage for Sunday is not an overkill, adding it has been their standard operating procedure during big events. Fajardo assured the rallyists police officers will observe maximum tolerance and respect the right of demonstrators to free speech. She also reminded rally organizers to police their own ranks from infiltrators who are out to sow violence. Fajardo said the PNP is on normal alert status but added that police commanders have the option to adjust their security alert based on the prevailing situation in their areas of responsibility. — Emmanuel Tupas Philstar.com is one of the most vibrant, opinionated, discerning communities of readers on cyberspace. articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — “This is not about vengeance. Duterte was arrested by authorities at Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA), where he was served a warrant from the International Criminal Court (ICC), as transmitted by the International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol). “Today, Duterte is being made to answer—not to me, but to the victims, to their families, to a world that refuses to forget,” she said. “I faced my case, knowing I was innocent. I stood before the courts because I had nothing to hide. Duterte now has to answer for his actions, not in the court of public opinion, but before the rule of law. This is how justice should work—those in power must be held to the same standards as everyone else,” she said. De Lima said Duterte’s arrest was “deeply personal” for her. She had been one of Duterte’s staunchest critics during his administration. In turn, Duterte accused her of involvement in the illegal drug trade, leading to her imprisonment for nearly seven years on what she maintained were trumped-up charges. “For almost seven years, I was imprisoned on fabricated charges, accused of crimes I did not commit—all because I dared to speak out against Duterte’s drug war.
